newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr dips vs yen in Tokyo on US official's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Dlr dips vs yen in Tokyo on US official's remarks.

text.p: 0620 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar softened against the yen by late Tokyo on Wednesday, partly depressed by comments by a U.S. official expressing concern over rises in Japan's current account surplus, dealers said.
But the downside was limited after Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura said the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) current low interest rate policy still has positive effects on the economy.

Lawrence Greenwood, economic minister-counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo, said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television that rises in Japan's current account surplus have the potential to create an explosive situation with the United States.
He added that the United States believes Japan's current account surplus will continue to rise into next year.

"The market ignored the trade data (released earlier). But his comments had an impact because traders had built long positions in the morning...and saw his comments as an opportunity to unwind their longs," a trust bank dealer said.

The market mostly shrugged off Japan's customs-cleared trade data for the first 20 days of July released early in the morning. The surplus rose 126.4 percent to 480.57 billion yen in the period compared with a revised surplus of 212.26 billion yen in the same period last year.
The dollar rose as high as 119.59 yen on purchases by U.S. securities firms, but its advance was capped by profit-taking, light exporter sales and option-related sales, dealers said.
But traders were still upbeat about the dollar's recent rally, with many believing that the greenback will eventually test the key psychological point of 120 yen in the near future.

"Unless the dollar falls below 118.50 yen, I think the dollar's bullish trend will continue," a dealer at a European bank said, adding that buying interest on dips below 119 yen will keep the dollar's downside solid.

Although the greenback dipped below 119 yen following Greenwood's comments, it managed to crawl back up above 119 yen again on short-covering, prompted by comments from Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura in the late afternoon, dealers said.
Komura said in an interview with Reuters: "We believe the effects of the low rate (policy) are spreading to various sectors (of the economy). It still has positive effects."
Dealers are waiting for possible comments on currencies from Haruhiko Kuroda, the recently appointed director-general of the Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau.
Kuroda will speak at a meeting at the Forex Club, which is scheduled to start at around 0930 GMT.

The trust bank dealer said he does not expect Kuroda to make any significant statements at the meeting since he already said on Wednesday that Japan's stance on the foreign exchange markets remains unchanged. But he added that dealers are curious to find out the new director-general's views on currencies, trade issues and Japan's interest rates.
The dollar hovered narrowly against the mark, but sentiment remained bullish after it hit a new 94-month peak overnight, dealers said.
The dollar closed at 119.20/30 yen and 1.8790/80 marks in New York on Tuesday.
--- Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8584
